bullets: Game index 4 of a seven-game session on one list (video 818.8s-998.7s). The in-game clock OCR failed for the entire video, so all timestamps here are video seconds and clock times are unknown.

The list has no small spell at all — Bomb Tower, Royal Delivery, Fire Spirit and Ice Spirit carry every swarm answer. In this game that shows as a Bomb Tower played four to five times (t=827.0 [8, 9], 907.9 [9, 9], 919.3 [7, 9], 947.9 [7, 9], 958.3), always in the central row-9 band and always cycled before the threat exists: "I'll cycle my bomb tower in the middle" (t=826), "Let's bomb tower here. Next skelly barrel will be evolved" (t=917-921).

Offence is a two-lane bait loop that never stops: six Goblin Barrels and six Wall Breakers between t=818.8 and t=980.0, alternating lanes ("Let's just split wall breakers again", t=880; "Let's go for the wall breakers opposite lane. Just keep up the pressure", t=973). Against a bait opponent the pairing is deliberately an elixir trap — "he has to double drop on defense or give us a wall breakers connection. Which he gives us the connection" (t=886-890).

The Magic Archer is the piece he says makes the list work, and it is always placed low in his own half (rows 7-9) so the piercing shot crosses the river from safety: "let's magic archer low here to take out the dark goblin" (t=865-868), "I do want to start abusing my magic archer really, really hard in this match" (t=944-948), then "Oh my god, the marcher's on the tower somehow. Three little three hits right there" (t=968-972).

Ronin is played strictly as defence in this game — [9, 1], [12, 6], [10, 6], all in his own half — used to pop a Suspicious Bush (t=912-914) and to Parry a Dart Goblin (t=957-958). He explicitly turns down a bridge Ronin on a read: "I kind of want to rowan at the bridge, but I feel like he has rascals. It wouldn't be that great of a play" (t=870-872), and his standing verdict is "there's a lot of just bait in the meta just making sure that the rowan never becomes solid" (t=849-854).

Damage management is one-sided by choice: he concedes chip on his left tower to save elixir ("I think I want to eat that, to be honest, cuz it's on my low lane tower anyways", t=909-912) and puts everything into the enemy right tower, which falls 4858 -> 144 HP while both of his own towers survive at 4135 and 4126.
Result: a win. Opponent appears to concede at t=994-998 — "I think he's just going to give up. Come on. Fire spirit. GG's. Perfect game" — though no victory screen or crown count was read.

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel, Wall Breakers and the two spirits all demand different cheap answers and are thrown in overlapping two-lane waves at 2.9 average elixir, with Bomb Tower and Royal Delivery — not a spell — doing the defending.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: This is log bait rebuilt without a log: the eight cards carry no small spell at all, so Bomb Tower, Royal Delivery, Fire Spirit and Ice Spirit have to cover every swarm, and in exchange both bait threats (Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers) can be thrown on cooldown instead of held. At 2.9 average elixir the pair comes back around faster than a bait opponent can double-answer, which is the trap Ryley names out loud: "he has to double drop on defense or give us a wall breakers connection" (t=886-890). Magic Archer is the value engine and is never bridged — placed at rows 7-9 in his own half it pierces across the river on defence and still chips the tower, which is where most of the closing damage came from ("the marcher's on the tower somehow. Three little three hits right there", t=968-972). Ronin is the mini-tank that lets a spell-less deck survive ground pushes: fast, and his Parry blocks and reflects a melee hit, which Ryley uses to pop a Suspicious Bush and to stop a Dart Goblin, but he keeps it entirely on his own half against swarm decks because Rascals or Goblins would eat a bridge commitment.
